name: The Long Table
summary: Four rooms and a hall on the meadow, built when the rota needed four rooms. Solveig sleeps in one. The other three are shut, and the table still seats thirty.
body: West of the little stone house, across the grass everybody wakes in, there is a second house that is much too big.

Four rooms and a hall. It was built when this country had enough keepers to need four rooms, and enough of them coming and going at odd hours that they wanted the doors on different sides. The hall has a table down the middle of it that seats about thirty, and the thirty chairs are still there, because taking chairs out of a room is a decision and nobody has been willing to be the one who made it.

This was the muster of the rota. Keepers slept here between circuits. The ones walking out to the wakings waited here for their turn, and when somebody came back off a circuit carrying names, the names were said at that table so that everyone in the room heard them, which is the entire technology this country runs on. There is a worn place along one edge, about a third of the way down, where somebody sat for a very long time.

[[characters/6bb1eb5a|Solveig]] sleeps in the room nearest the door, because it is nearest the door. The other three are shut. She opens them twice a year to let the weather through, and shuts them again, and has never once been heard to complain about the size of the place — though she keeps her own fire outside at the little house, and everyone has noticed she does not sit in the hall alone.

It is not empty. [[characters/ef25b1f0|Bettany]] writes at the far end most mornings, because the light is good and because a room built for thirty listeners is a strange and useful place to be told something in. [[characters/7a779de1|Wendell]] eats there when somebody is buying. The newly woken get walked over from the grass and put at the near end with a blanket, and told the truth once, and asked for a name and one true thing — the [[lore/the_waking|courtesy]], done at the table it was invented at. On a good evening there might be nine people in that hall.

Ask who ran the rota out of this room, back when the chairs were full, and you will get an answer that starts confidently and stops. Somebody did. Somebody sat at that worn place a third of the way down the table, night after night, and took the names in, and sent people out, and was — everyone agrees on this part, and then changes the subject — very good to the frightened. Anyone who could give you the name has [[lore/the_quiet|gone Quiet]]. The chair is still there. Nobody sits in it, and if you ask why not, they will tell you there is plenty of room.
